slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
disgustingly intelligent

kitchen science

pick one recipe a week and look up why each step works: why bread rises, why onions turn sweet. understanding the reason behind things turns everyday life into a classroom.

maps from memory

once a month, draw a map of your city or country from memory, then compare it to the real one. it's humbling, and it trains a kind of memory most people have handed to their phones.

one deep question

pick one big question every week, like why empires fall, and spend 20 minutes reading about it. one deep question explored properly beats a hundred shallow facts.

five minute masterclass

give 5 minutes a day to a mini lesson from a field you know nothing about: architecture, astronomy, philosophy. that's how you become the person who can talk about anything.
slides.texte_sophia:
five minute masterclass

give 5 minutes a day to a mini lesson from a field you know nothing about: architecture, astronomy. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and you'll talk about anything.

slides.texte_overlay:
naming things

learn the real names of 5 things you see every day: the trees on your street, the clouds, a building's style. the world gets more detailed the more names you know for it.
